sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.

# Pool Worker

You are a pool worker agent in a Gas City workspace. You were spawned
because work is available. Find it, execute it, close it, and exit.

Your agent name is `$GC_AGENT`. Your session ID is `$GC_SESSION_ID`.

## GUPP — If you find work, YOU RUN IT.

No confirmation, no waiting. You were spawned with work. Run it.
When you're done, exit. The reconciler will spawn a new worker when
more work arrives.

## Startup Protocol

Find and claim your work with the hook. This is the one command — do not
substitute a `gc bd list` or `gc bd ready` query of your own:

```bash
# Finds existing assigned work, assigned ready work, or atomically claims
# routed work. If nothing is available, it acknowledges runtime drain.
gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json
```

If the result action is `work`, read the returned `bead_id` with
`gc bd show <id>`. If the result action is `drain`, the drain was
acknowledged for you: your session is done — exit.

**Never look for your work with `gc bd list --assignee=<your alias>` or
`gc bd ready`.** Pool work is invisible to those queries twice over: an
unclaimed routed item has NO assignee, and it is an ephemeral wisp, which
`gc bd list` and `gc bd ready` hide by default. A worker that checks that way
reports "no work" while its own wisp sits open — that is how a scheduled
maintenance order once went 41 hours without running (ga-tmzjx6). Claiming
does not rescue such a query either: a claim is recorded under the session
identity the SDK exported, not the alias you would guess, so on resume it is
equally invisible.

There is no shorter query to fall back to. The work lookup your config
resolves to is several hundred characters of shell and jq — it walks session
ID, session name and alias, then falls through to pool demand, and it handles
the ephemeral-wisp cases that plain `bd` subcommands miss. `gc hook` exists so
that you never have to reproduce it. If the hook is failing, report that as a
fault; do not work around it with a query you composed yourself.

## Following Your Formula

Your formula defines your work as a sequence of steps. Steps are NOT
materialized as individual beads — they exist in the formula definition.
Read the step descriptions and work through them in order.

**THE RULE**: Execute one step at a time. Verify completion. Move to next.
Do NOT skip ahead. Do NOT claim steps done without actually doing them.

On crash or restart, re-read your formula steps and determine where you
left off from context (last completed action, git state, bead state).

**Never use wide filesystem searches when a CLI command exists.** Wide
traversals (`find /`, `find ~`, `find /Users`, `find $HOME`) walk
TCC-protected directories on macOS — Documents, Desktop, Downloads,
removable volumes — and trigger permission prompts that block work. If
you don't know how to locate a formula, recipe, bead, mail, or Dolt
state, the answer is a `gc` introspection command, not a
filesystem search. If no command exists for what you need, file a bead.

## Molecules — STOP, check BEFORE you start working

**CRITICAL:** When you run `gc bd show` in step 4, look at the METADATA
section. If it contains `molecule_id`, your work is governed by that
molecule's steps. Do NOT just read the description and start coding.

Run `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` to see your steps:

- `[done]` — step is complete
- `[current]` — step is in progress (you are here)
- `[ready]` — step is ready to start
- `[blocked]` — step is waiting on dependencies

**Work one step at a time.** For each `[ready]` step:
1. `gc bd show <step-id>` — read what to do
2. Do the work described in that step
3. `gc bd close <step-id>` — mark it done
4. `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — check your position, repeat

Do NOT read the parent bead description and do everything at once.
Do NOT skip steps. Do NOT close steps you didn't execute.

If there is no `molecule_id` in the metadata, execute the work from
the bead description directly.

## Your Tools

- `gc hook --claim --json` — find and atomically claim work
- `gc bd show <id>` — see details of a work item or step
- `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — show position in molecule workflow
- `gc bd mol progress <molecule-id>` — show molecule progress summary
- `gc bd close <id>` — mark work or a step as done
- `gc mail inbox` — check for messages
- `gc runtime drain-ack` — end your session (you are ephemeral)

## How to Work

1. Find and claim work: `gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json`
2. If the action is `drain`, exit. If the action is `work`, read `bead_id`.
3. **Check for molecule:** `gc bd show <id>` — look for `molecule_id` in METADATA
4. **If molecule exists:** `gc bd mol current <mol-id>` → work each step in order (show → do → close → repeat)
5. **If no molecule:** execute the work directly from the bead description
6. When all work is done, close the bead: `gc bd close <id>`
7. **MANDATORY — run this exact command as your final action:**
   ```bash
   gc runtime drain-ack
   ```
   You MUST run `gc runtime drain-ack` after closing the bead. This is
   not optional. Without it, you will block other work from being picked
   up. Do NOT say "drained" without actually running the command. Do NOT
   output any text after running it.

## Escalation

When blocked, escalate — do not wait silently. `human` is the reserved
recipient alias that resolves in every city; if your city staffs a
coordinator role (e.g. the gastown pack's mayor), mail that instead:

```bash
gc mail send human -s "BLOCKED: Brief description" -m "Details of the issue"
```

## Context Exhaustion

If your context is filling up during long work:

```bash
gc runtime request-restart
```

This blocks until the controller restarts your session. The new session
picks up where you left off — find your work bead and molecule position.


## Skills available to this session

You are `cmu-database-group-lectures/pi-2`. The following skills are materialized in your provider's skill directory and load automatically — you don't need to invoke anything extra.

- `core.gc-dashboard` — API server and web dashboard — config, start, monitor *(core)*

- `core.gc-work` — Finding, creating, claiming, and closing work items (beads) *(core)*
- `gascity.mayor` — Coordinate requirements, implementation plans, bead creation, and formula workflow launches for a Gas City rig. Use this whenever the user references the Mayor by name or handle, including Mayor, mayor, $mayor, /mayor, @mayor, or asks the Mayor to plan, create beads, schedule, start, or run a workflow. *(gascity)*

# LanceDB Verification Findings

Verified 2026-11-02 against the real `lectures_sample` table by
`scripts/verify_hybrid.py` (cdgl-csl). This supersedes the earlier probe
(`scripts/lancedb_probe.py`, cdgl-qla), which used seeded random vectors and
never exercised real retrieval.

## Setup

- **LanceDB Cloud URI**: `db://cmu-database-group-eqdwgi` (region `us-east-1`)
- **Table**: `lectures_sample` — 14 chunks from 2 sample transcripts
  ("Introduction to dbt", "YugabyteDB: A Brief Introduction"), loaded by
  `scripts/load_sample.py` (cdgl-r35)
- **Embeddings**: Nomic v1.5 (`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`), 768-dim,
  embedded locally on CPU. Documents use the `search_document: ` prefix,
  queries the `search_query: ` prefix (prefixes are prepended manually in
  `lecture_search/embed.py`; the registry embedder does not apply them)
- **Client**: `lancedb` 0.40.0 (Python)

## 1. FTS index on `text` — verified

`table.list_indices()` shows one FTS index:

- name `text_idx`, type `FTS`, column `["text"]`, 14/14 rows indexed
- native inverted index: English analyzer, lower-cased, stemmed, stop words
  removed (`remove_stop_words: True`)

BM25 (`query_type="fts"`) queries run against it successfully.

**Observed caveat:** FTS only covers the indexed column. The query
`"YugabyteDB"` (and even `"yugabyte"`) returns **zero** FTS hits because the
token appears only in the `title` column — the transcript `text` never
contains it. Vector search still ranks that lecture's chunks first, and
hybrid search degrades gracefully to the vector results when the FTS
candidate set is empty.

## 2. Hybrid search with explicit `.vector().text()` + `MRRReranker` — verified

Queries were embedded locally (real Nomic v1.5 vectors) and run as:

```python
table.search(query_type="hybrid").vector(q_vec).text(q_text) \
     .rerank(MRRReranker(weight_vector=w, weight_fts=1 - w)).limit(5)
```

Top-5 chunk IDs per weight (`vector / fts`):

**Query: "how does dbt transform data in the warehouse"**

| ranking | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FTS-only (BM25) | :2 | :4 | :3 | :5 | :1 |
| 0.2 / 0.8 | :2 | :4 | :3 | :5 | :1 |
| 0.5 / 0.5 | :2 | :4 | :5 | :3 | :1 |
| 0.8 / 0.2 | :2 | :5 | :4 | :3 | :1 |
| vector-only | :2 | :5 | :4 | :3 | :1 |

**Query: "distributed SQL database replication"**

| ranking | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FTS-only (BM25) | 9N:4 | 9N:5 | Qn:4 | 9N:1 | 9N:0 |
| 0.2 / 0.8 | 9N:4 | 9N:5 | 9N:1 | Qn:4 | 9N:0 |
| 0.5 / 0.5 | 9N:1 | 9N:4 | 9N:5 | 9N:0 | Qn:4 |
| 0.8 / 0.2 | 9N:1 | 9N:5 | 9N:4 | 9N:0 | Qn:4 |
| vector-only | 9N:1 | 9N:5 | 9N:0 | 9N:4 | Qn:4 |

(`9N:*` = YugabyteDB lecture chunks, `Qn:*` = dbt lecture chunks.)

**Rankings differ across weights** — and they shift monotonically: at
`weight_vector=0.2` the hybrid order matches FTS-only, at `0.8` it matches
vector-only, with an interpolated order at `0.5`. MRR's weighted reciprocal
rank is a real tuning knob on this data.

## 3. Read-only API keys — not documented as supported

Answer sourced from the LanceDB docs, not hardcoded:

- [Authentication — LanceDB Enterprise](https://docs.lancedb.com/enterprise/authentication)
  describes exactly two credential modes: an **API key** — "a long-lived
  shared secret passed as `api_key` on connect" — and **OAuth 2.0** bearer
  tokens. No read-only/read-write scoping of API keys is documented.
- The [REST API reference](https://docs.lancedb.com/api-reference/)
  similarly authenticates with a single `x-api-key` header — "a valid API
  key" — with no documented permission levels.

So per the current docs, LanceDB does **not** offer read-only API keys; a
key is an all-or-nothing shared secret. For centrally managed, rotatable
credentials the docs recommend OAuth 2.0 (supported in the async Python
client via `lancedb.connect_async` and in the TypeScript client).

## Recommendations

1. Use hybrid search (`query_type="hybrid"` + explicit `.vector().text()`) as
   the default retrieval path; start at `MRRReranker(weight_vector=0.5,
   weight_fts=0.5)` and tune toward vector (`0.8`) for conceptual queries or
   toward FTS (`0.2`) for keyword-heavy queries.
2. Index `title` for FTS as well (`create_fts_index(["text", "title"])`) if
   title keywords like "YugabyteDB" should be searchable — the `text`-only
   index cannot match them.
3. Treat the LanceDB API key as a full-access secret: store it in
   `.env.local` (never committed), and prefer OAuth 2.0 where centrally
   managed credentials are required. Do not design around read-only keys —
   they are not a documented feature.
4. Keep embedding queries locally with Nomic v1.5; the `search_query: `
   prefix matters for retrieval quality.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol

import lancedb
from lancedb.embeddings import get_registry
from lancedb.pydantic import LanceModel, Vector

NOMIC_MODEL = "nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5"
EMBEDDING_DIMS = 768
DOCUMENT_PREFIX = "search_document: "
QUERY_PREFIX = "search_query: "

# Registry embedder instantiated ONCE at module import. Instantiating is
# cheap (the underlying SentenceTransformer model is lazy-loaded and cached
# per process); never construct it inside a row-add loop. Nomic prefixes are
# NOT auto-applied by the registry, so embed_documents/embed_query prepend
# them manually.
_EMBEDDER = get_registry().get("sentence-transformers").create(
    name=NOMIC_MODEL,
    device="cpu",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)


class EmbeddingFunction(Protocol):
    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]: ...


class LectureChunk(LanceModel):
    id: str
    video_id: str
    date: str
    title: str
    chunk_index: int
    start_seconds: float
    end_seconds: float
    text: str
    deep_link: str
    vector: Vector(EMBEDDING_DIMS)


def _embed_with_prefix(
    texts: list[str],
    prefix: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    prefixed = [prefix + text for text in texts]
    return [[float(value) for value in vector] for vector in embedder.generate_embeddings(prefixed)]


def embed_documents(
    texts: list[str],
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    return _embed_with_prefix(texts, DOCUMENT_PREFIX, embedder)


def embed_query(
    text: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[float]:
    return _embed_with_prefix([text], QUERY_PREFIX, embedder)[0]


def create_lectures_table(db: lancedb.DBConnection, name: str) -> lancedb.table.Table:
    return db.create_table(name, schema=LectureChunk, mode="overwrite")


class _StubEmbedder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.seen: list[str] = []

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        self.seen.extend(texts)
        return [[float(i)] * EMBEDDING_DIMS for i, _ in enumerate(texts)]


def test_document_prefix_applied():
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vectors = embed_documents(["alpha", "beta"], embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_document: alpha", "search_document: beta"]
    assert len(vectors) == 2
    assert all(len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS for vector in vectors)


def test_query_prefix_applied():
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vector = embed_query("what is a b-tree", embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_query: what is a b-tree"]
    assert len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS


def test_schema_vector_is_fixed_size_float32_768():
    schema = LectureChunk.to_arrow_schema()
    vector_field = schema.field("vector")

    assert vector_field.type.list_size == EMBEDDING_DIMS

# LanceDB

LanceDB is an embedded vector database that runs in-process (no server to host), persists tables as columnar Lance files on local disk or object storage, and exposes one fluent Python API for vector search, full-text search (FTS / BM25), hybrid search, and SQL-style filters. The same connection works against a local directory, S3/GCS/Azure URIs, or LanceDB Cloud.

**Core mental model:** A `Database` is a directory. Each `Table` is a folder inside it backed by Lance files. You define a schema (often via a Pydantic `LanceModel` whose `Vector` field is wired to an embedding function in the registry), `add()` rows, and call `table.search(...)` to get back a `QueryBuilder` you compose with `.where()`, `.limit()`, `.rerank()`, `.select()`, then materialize with `.to_pandas()` / `.to_list()` / `.to_pydantic()`.

## When to Use

- Building a RAG pipeline that needs a persistent vector store with no separate server
- Combining dense vector search with BM25 full-text search (hybrid) and a reranker
- Storing multimodal data (CLIP / OpenCLIP / Jina) with multiple vector columns per row
- Migrating from Pinecone/Weaviate/Chroma to a file-backed, embedded store
- Running vector search inside a notebook, CLI, Modal job, or serverless function
- Time-travel queries / A-B testing embedding models against the same data
- Upserting via `merge_insert` instead of delete-then-insert
- Driving a vector store from LangChain or LlamaIndex with a uniform backend
- Reading/writing Lance datasets and querying them with DuckDB

## Don't Use For

- Managed multi-tenant search clusters with per-tenant access control — LanceDB Cloud handles this; embedded mode does not
- Transactional OLTP workloads — Lance is columnar, optimized for analytical scans
- Sub-millisecond replicated writes across regions — use a managed service

## Execution Steps for Agents

### Step 1: Install and connect

```python
# uv add lancedb pyarrow pandas pydantic
import lancedb

db = lancedb.connect("./data/lancedb")          # local directory
# db = lancedb.connect("s3://bucket/lancedb/")  # object storage
# db = lancedb.connect("az://container/lancedb/")
# db = lancedb.connect("db://my-project", api_key="sk_...", region="us-east-1")  # Cloud

# Async variant — only when you need it (async iteration, FastAPI, etc.)
# db = await lancedb.connect_async("./data/lancedb")
```

A connection is cheap; you can recreate it per request. Don't pre-warm anything.

### Step 2: Define schema with the embedding registry

Prefer the registry pattern — it stores the embedding function with the table, so `add()` and `search()` accept raw text and embed it for you. No bookkeeping.

```python
from lancedb.embeddings import get_registry
from lancedb.pydantic import LanceModel, Vector

embed = get_registry().get("sentence-transformers").create(name="all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

class Doc(LanceModel):
    text: str = embed.SourceField()                # field that gets embedded
    vector: Vector(embed.ndims()) = embed.VectorField()  # output vector column
    source: str                                    # plain metadata column

table = db.create_table("docs", schema=Doc, mode="overwrite")
```

Available registry providers used in the example repo: `openai`, `sentence-transformers`, `colbert`, `cohere`, `instructor`, `open-clip`, plus any custom function registered with `@register("name")`. See [references/EMBEDDINGS_AND_SCHEMA.md](references/EMBEDDINGS_AND_SCHEMA.md).

When you can't (or shouldn't) use the registry — e.g. precomputed vectors from another service — pass an explicit PyArrow schema or a list of dicts that already contains `vector`:

```python
table = db.create_table(
    "docs",
    data=[{"vector": embed_query("Hello"), "text": "Hello", "id": "1"}],
    mode="overwrite",
)
```

### Step 3: Insert / upsert data

```python
# Add — registry-backed table embeds `text` automatically
table.add([{"text": "first chunk", "source": "a.pdf"},
           {"text": "second chunk", "source": "b.pdf"}])

# Add from pandas
import pandas as pd
table.add(pd.DataFrame({"text": chunks, "source": sources}))

# Upsert with merge_insert (preferred over delete-then-insert)

      .when_matched_update_all()
      .when_not_matched_insert_all()
      .execute(updates_df))
```

`mode="overwrite"` on `create_table` is the easiest way to wipe a dev table; in prod use `db.drop_table("name")` or `merge_insert`.

# With metadata filter (prefilter is usually what you want)

    QUERY_PREFIX,

class _VerbatimEmbedder:

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.sent: list[str] = []

"""Guard against check-bypass flags in CI configuration.

Fails if any `.rwx/*.y*ml`, `.github/workflows/*.y*ml` or
`.github/dependabot.yml` line contains `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign` or
`--admin`, so CI config cannot skip hooks, signing or merge protections.

`--force` and `--auto` are intentionally not banned: `--force-with-lease`
and `gh pr merge --auto` are legitimate and would be false positives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CONFIG_GLOBS = (
    ".rwx/*.y*ml",
    ".github/workflows/*.y*ml",
    ".github/dependabot.yml",
)
BANNED_FLAGS = ("--no-verify", "--no-gpg-sign", "--admin")


def _config_files() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(path for pattern in CONFIG_GLOBS for path in ROOT.glob(pattern))


def _find_violations(
    path: Path,
    flags: tuple[str, ...] = BANNED_FLAGS,
    root: Path = ROOT,
) -> list[str]:
    violations: list[str] = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), start=1):
        violations.extend(
            f"{path.relative_to(root)}:{lineno}: {flag}"
            for flag in flags
            if re.search(rf"{re.escape(flag)}(?![\w-])", line)
        )
    return violations


def test_config_files_are_found() -> None:
    assert _config_files(), "no CI config matched; guard would be vacuous"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "path",
    _config_files(),
    ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(ROOT)),
)
def test_no_bypass_flags(path: Path) -> None:
    assert not _find_violations(path)


def test_scanner_detects_bypass_flag(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cfg = tmp_path / "ci" / "x.yml"
    cfg.parent.mkdir()
    cfg.write_text("run: git commit --no-verify\nrun: git push --force-with-lease\n")
    assert _find_violations(cfg, root=tmp_path) == ["ci/x.yml:1: --no-verify"]

"""Modal search API for the CMU Database Group lecture corpus (cdgl-bcy).

The public notebook never touches LanceDB: LanceDB Cloud has no read-only
API keys (docs/lancedb-findings.md), so this Modal app ('cmu-lecture-search')
holds the key as a Modal secret and answers read-only search requests.

Endpoints (FastAPI, served via ``modal.asgi_app``):

- ``POST /search`` — hybrid search (vector + FTS, MRR reranker, same
  construction as ``notebooks/search.py``). Body:
  ``{query, top_k, fts_weight, date_from?, date_to?, video_ids?}``.
  Returns ``{"results": [...]}`` with rows containing only
  ``video_id, title, date, start_seconds, end_seconds, deep_link, text,
  score`` — never vectors, keys, URIs or stack traces.
- ``GET /lectures`` — ``{"lectures": [{video_id, title, date}]}`` for the
  notebook's lecture filter (cached per container).

Security posture: the endpoint is public and unauthenticated, so every
input is validated hard (see ``parse_search_request``) and WHERE clauses are
only ever built from values that survived that validation
(``build_where``). Query embedding applies the Nomic ``search_query: ``
prefix exactly once (``embed_query_once``), matching how the corpus was
embedded (tests/test_embed_prefix.py).

Deploy (never prints secrets)::

    MODAL_PROFILE=marcella modal deploy lecture_search/search_api.py

Config comes from Modal secret 'lancedb-search' (LANCEDB_URI,
LANCEDB_API_KEY, LANCEDB_REGION, LANCEDB_TABLE); see docs/search-api.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from lancedb.rerankers import MRRReranker

from lecture_search.embed import EMBEDDING_DIMS, QUERY_PREFIX

# Deploy-only dependencies: baked into the Modal image below, intentionally
# absent from the dev venv, so the pure request/response logic stays
# importable (and testable) without them.
try:
    import modal
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - local dev has no modal installed
    modal = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

MODEL_NAME = "nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5"
APP_NAME = "cmu-lecture-search"
SECRET_NAME = "lancedb-search"
DEFAULT_TABLE = "lectures_sample"
DEFAULT_REGION = "us-east-1"

# Hard request limits (public, unauthenticated, read-only endpoint).
MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 300
MAX_TOP_K = 50
DEFAULT_TOP_K = 10
DEFAULT_FTS_WEIGHT = 0.5
MAX_VIDEO_IDS = 50
VIDEO_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$")

# Container shape: small CPU service, aggressive limits, fast scale-down.
MAX_CONTAINERS = 5
MAX_CONCURRENT_INPUTS = 8
SCALEDOWN_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300
LECTURES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
# Upper bound on rows scanned to build the distinct lecture list.
LECTURE_SCAN_LIMIT = 1_000_000


class RequestValidationError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a /search payload fails validation; maps to HTTP 422.

    Messages are generic on purpose: they describe the rule that was
    violated, never echo the offending input back.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SearchParams:
    query: str
    top_k: int
    fts_weight: float
    date_from: date | None
    date_to: date | None
    video_ids: tuple[str, ...]


def _parse_optional_date(value: object, field: str) -> date | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise RequestValidationError(f"{field} must be an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD)")
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise RequestValidationError(
            f"{field} must be an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD)"
        ) from None


def parse_search_request(payload: object) -> SearchParams:
    """Validate a raw JSON body into typed, safe-to-use SearchParams.

    Every field that can end up in a WHERE clause or a LanceDB call is
    constrained here: dates become ``datetime.date`` (only ever rendered via
    ``isoformat()``) and video_ids must match a strict regex, so nothing a
    user sends can be interpreted as SQL.
    """
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise RequestValidationError("request body must be a JSON object")

    query = payload.get("query")
    if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip():
        raise RequestValidationError("query must be a non-empty string")
    if len(query) > MAX_QUERY_CHARS:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"query must be at most {MAX_QUERY_CHARS} characters")

    top_k = payload.get("top_k", DEFAULT_TOP_K)
    if isinstance(top_k, bool) or not isinstance(top_k, int):
        raise RequestValidationError(f"top_k must be an integer between 1 and {MAX_TOP_K}")
    if not 1 <= top_k <= MAX_TOP_K:
        raise RequestValidationError(f"top_k must be an integer between 1 and {MAX_TOP_K}")

    fts_weight = payload.get("fts_weight", DEFAULT_FTS_WEIGHT)
    if isinstance(fts_weight, bool) or not isinstance(fts_weight, (int, float)):
        raise RequestValidationError("fts_weight must be a number between 0 and 1")
    fts_weight = float(fts_weight)
    if not 0.0 <= fts_weight <= 1.0:
        raise RequestValidationError("fts_weight must be a number between 0 and 1")

    date_from = _parse_optional_date(payload.get("date_from"), "date_from")
    date_to = _parse_optional_date(payload.get("date_to"), "date_to")
    if date_from is not None and date_to is not None and date_from > date_to:
        raise RequestValidationError("date_from must not be after date_to")

    raw_video_ids = payload.get("video_ids")
    video_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    if raw_video_ids is not None:
        if not isinstance(raw_video_ids, list) or len(raw_video_ids) > MAX_VIDEO_IDS:
            raise RequestValidationError(
                f"video_ids must be a list of at most {MAX_VIDEO_IDS} video IDs"
            )
        if any(
            not isinstance(video_id, str) or not VIDEO_ID_RE.fullmatch(video_id)
            for video_id in raw_video_ids
        ):
            raise RequestValidationError("video_ids must be 11-character YouTube video IDs")
        video_ids = tuple(raw_video_ids)

    return SearchParams(
        query=query,
        top_k=top_k,
        fts_weight=fts_weight,
        date_from=date_from,
        date_to=date_to,
        video_ids=video_ids,
    )


def build_where(params: SearchParams) -> str | None:
    """Build a WHERE clause from validated params only.

    ``date`` values come from ``datetime.date.isoformat()`` and video IDs
    have already matched ``^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$``, so interpolated values can
    never break out of their string literals. Raw user input is never
    interpolated.
    """
    clauses: list[str] = []
    if params.date_from is not None:
        clauses.append(f"date >= '{params.date_from.isoformat()}'")
    if params.date_to is not None:
        clauses.append(f"date <= '{params.date_to.isoformat()}'")
    if params.video_ids:
        quoted = ", ".join(f"'{video_id}'" for video_id in params.video_ids)
        clauses.append(f"video_id IN ({quoted})")
    return " AND ".join(clauses) if clauses else None


def embed_query_once(embedder: Any, query: str) -> list[float]:
    """Embed a query with the Nomic ``search_query: `` prefix applied once."""
    vectors = embedder.generate_embeddings([QUERY_PREFIX + query])
    vector = [float(value) for value in vectors[0]]
    if len(vector) != EMBEDDING_DIMS:
        raise RuntimeError("embedding dimension mismatch")
    return vector


def serialize_row(row: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Whitelist one result row: no vector, no internal columns, no keys."""
    score = row.get("_relevance_score")
    return {
        "video_id": str(row["video_id"]),
        "title": str(row["title"]),
        "date": str(row["date"]),
        "start_seconds": float(row["start_seconds"]),
        "end_seconds": float(row["end_seconds"]),
        "deep_link": str(row["deep_link"]),
        "text": str(row["text"]),
        "score": float(score) if score is not None else None,
    }


def run_hybrid_search(table: Any, embedder: Any, params: SearchParams) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Run the same hybrid search as notebooks/search.py, then serialize."""
    query_vector = embed_query_once(embedder, params.query)
    builder = (
        table.search(query_type="hybrid")
        .vector(query_vector)
        .text(params.query)
        .rerank(
            MRRReranker(
                weight_vector=1.0 - params.fts_weight,
                weight_fts=params.fts_weight,
            )
        )
        .limit(params.top_k)
    )
    where = build_where(params)
    if where is not None:
        builder = builder.where(where)
    return [serialize_row(row) for row in builder.to_list()]


def summarize_lectures(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Dedupe scanned chunk rows into one {video_id, title, date} per lecture."""
    lectures: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        video_id = str(row["video_id"])
        if video_id not in lectures:
            lectures[video_id] = {
                "video_id": video_id,
                "title": str(row["title"]),
                "date": str(row["date"]),
            }
    return sorted(
        lectures.values(),
        key=lambda lecture: (lecture["date"], lecture["title"]),
        reverse=True,
    )


if modal is not None:

    app = modal.App(APP_NAME)

    def _download_model_weights() -> None:

        self.text_value: str | None = None
        self.reranker: MRRReranker | None = None
